Cebuano

[edit]

[edit]

lago

Anagrams

Esperanto

[edit]
Esperanto Wikipedia has an article on:
lago
Wikipedia eo

Etymology

[edit]

From Italian lago. Doublet of laguno.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈlaɡo/
  • Audio 1:(file)
  • Audio 2:(file)
  • Audio 3:(file)
  • Rhymes: -aɡo
  • Syllabification: la‧go

Noun

[edit]

lago (accusative singular lagon, plural lagoj, accusative plural lagojn)

  1. lake

Derived terms

[edit]
  • lageto (“pond”)

Further reading

[edit]
  • “lago”, in Plena Ilustrita Vortaro de Esperanto [Complete Illustrated Dictionary of Esperanto], 2020, →ISBN
  • “lago”, in Reta Vortaro [Online Dictionary] (in Esperanto), 1997-present

Fijian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Central-Pacific *laŋo, from Proto-Oceanic *laŋo, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *laŋaw.

Noun

[edit]

lago

  1. fly

Galician

[edit]
Galician Wikipedia has an article on:
lago
Wikipedia gl

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Galician-Portuguese lago, from Latin lacus (“lake”), from Proto-Indo-European *lókus (“lake, pool”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • IPA(key): /ˈlaɡo/ [ˈlɑ.ɣ̞ʊ]
  • IPA(key): (standard) /ˈlaɡo/ [ˈlɑ.ɣ̞ʊ]
  • IPA(key): (gheada) /ˈlaħo/ [ˈlɑ.ħʊ]

 
  • Rhymes: -aɡo
  • Rhymes: -aɡo
  • Rhymes: -aħo

  • Hyphenation: la‧go

Noun

[edit]

lago m (plural lagos)

  1. lake, pool, pond
  2. water reservoir

Derived terms

[edit]
  • Lago
  • Lagos

Related terms

[edit]
  • asolagar
  • lagar
  • lagoa
  • lagorza

[edit]

  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, editor (2006–2013), “lago”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios da lingua galega [Dictionary of Dictionaries of the Galician language] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, Ernesto Xosé González Seoane, María Álvarez de la Granja, editors (2003–2018), “lago”, in Tesouro informatizado da lingua galega (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega

  • Rhymes: -aɡu
  • Hyphenation: la‧go

Noun

[edit]

lago m (plural lagos)

  1. lake

Tagalog

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

From Proto-Philippine *lagúq (“to flourish, of plants”). Possibly related to Sanskrit लघु (laghú, “well; in good health; healthy”). Compare Pangasinan lago (“healthy; robust individual”) and Kapampangan lagu (“beauty; tenderness of plants”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Tagalog) IPA(key): /laˈɡoʔ/ [lɐˈɣoʔ]
  • Rhymes: -oʔ
  • Syllabification: la‧go

Noun

[edit]

lagô (Baybayin spelling ᜎᜄᜓ)

  1. growth of plants
    Synonyms: tubo, pagtubo
  2. luxuriant growth
    Synonyms: yabong, pagyabong, lamba, paglamba
  3. (figurative) progress; development; growth
    Synonyms: unlad, pag-unlad, progreso
  4. parrot seed or wild saffron
Derived terms
[edit]
  • di-lumalago
  • ilago
  • kalaguan
  • lumago
  • malago
  • palaguin
See also
[edit]
  • kasubha

Etymology 2

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Tagalog) IPA(key): /ˈlaɡo/ [ˈlaː.ɣo]
  • Rhymes: -aɡo
  • Syllabification: la‧go

Noun

[edit]

lago (Baybayin spelling ᜎᜄᜓ)

  1. full or whole length
  2. entire piece; whole bolt (of cloth)
    Synonyms: piyesa, bulto, balumbon
  3. entire or full distance
  4. entirety; completeness
    Synonym: kabuoan

Etymology 3

[edit]

Borrowed from Spanish lago.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Tagalog) IPA(key): /ˈlaɡo/ [ˈlaː.ɣo]
  • Rhymes: -aɡo
  • Syllabification: la‧go

Noun

[edit]

lago (Baybayin spelling ᜎᜄᜓ)

  1. lake
    Synonyms: lawa, laguna, dagatan, lanaw

Further reading

[edit]
  • “lago”, in Pambansang Diksiyonaryo | Diksiyonaryo.ph, 2018

Anagrams

[edit]
  • laog, alog
